feedback.problem: Find the range of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of two intervals:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty )
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty )
$$

We can split this into two inequalities:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\le -1,\,\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\ge 1
$$

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

- If we add $1$ to the first interval, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\le -1 \\  & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+1\le -1+1 \\  & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+1\le 0 \\  & f(x)\le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

- If we add $1$ to the second interval, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\ge 1 \\  & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+1\ge 1+1 \\  & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+1\ge 2 \\  & f(x)\ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining both inequalities, we get

$$
f(x)\le 0,\,f(x)\ge 2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,0]\cup [2,\infty ).$
